description: Distributed consensus decomposed. Raft's leader election + log replication + safety. Paxos's basic protocol + Multi-Paxos. The FLP impossibility. CRDTs as a different approach. Modern variants: EPaxos, Flexible Paxos.

sub_mechanisms.name: leader_election
sub_mechanisms.definition: Raft: nodes start as followers. After election timeout, become candidate; request votes. Majority votes → leader.
sub_mechanisms.why: Single leader simplifies log replication. Random election timeouts prevent split votes. Leader serialises all writes — strong order.

sub_mechanisms.name: term_number
sub_mechanisms.definition: Raft: monotonic per-election integer. Each election bumps term. Servers compare terms to identify stale leaders.
sub_mechanisms.why: Detects + ignores stale leaders. Higher-term message from any server → current term updates. Foundation of safety: stale leaders can't commit.

sub_mechanisms.name: log_replication
sub_mechanisms.definition: Leader appends client command to log; replicates to followers via AppendEntries RPC. Command committed when majority acknowledge.
sub_mechanisms.why: Replicated log is the source of truth. Each node applies committed log entries to its state machine. Foundation of all log-based consensus.

sub_mechanisms.name: majority_quorum
sub_mechanisms.definition: Decisions need majority (⌈N/2⌉+1). 3 nodes: 2; 5 nodes: 3. Any two quorums intersect — ensures committed entries survive.
sub_mechanisms.why: Intersection property is the safety mechanism. New leader's quorum overlaps with prior committed-entries quorum → sees them. Without majority, two disjoint sub-quorums could commit conflicting entries.

sub_mechanisms.name: log_matching_property
sub_mechanisms.definition: Raft invariant: if two logs contain entry with same index + term, then everything before is identical.
sub_mechanisms.why: Simplifies AppendEntries: leader sends (prevLogIndex, prevLogTerm); follower rejects if mismatch. Leader retries with earlier index. Self-correcting replication.

sub_mechanisms.name: FLP_impossibility
sub_mechanisms.definition: Fischer-Lynch-Paterson 1985: no deterministic consensus algorithm tolerates one crash in asynchronous network.
sub_mechanisms.why: Theoretical bound. Practical algorithms (Raft, Paxos) use timeouts (partial synchrony) to make progress. FLP says: can't have safety + liveness + 1 crash in pure async. Real systems compromise on async assumption.

sub_mechanisms.name: Paxos_basic_protocol
sub_mechanisms.definition: Two phases: prepare (propose ballot number; learn highest accepted value) + accept (propose value; majority accept).
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundational consensus. Each round: phase 1 (read prior state) + phase 2 (write new). Multi-Paxos amortises phase 1 across many decisions.

sub_mechanisms.name: Multi_Paxos_optimisation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Stable leader skips phase 1 (one elected) for many decisions. Just phase 2 per decision.
sub_mechanisms.why: Phase 1 expensive (consult majority). Multi-Paxos amortises across N decisions. Closer to Raft in effective protocol but trickier to specify correctly.

sub_mechanisms.name: Byzantine_fault_tolerance
sub_mechanisms.definition: BFT protocols (PBFT, HotStuff) tolerate malicious nodes, not just crashes. Need ≥3f+1 nodes for f Byzantine.
sub_mechanisms.why: Permissioned blockchains, high-security systems. More expensive than crash-tolerant. Bitcoin/Ethereum use different (proof-of-work/stake) approaches; classical BFT used in HotStuff, PBFT.

sub_mechanisms.name: EPaxos_leaderless
sub_mechanisms.definition: Egalitarian Paxos: no fixed leader; each command picks coordinator. Geo-distributed performance.
sub_mechanisms.why: Leader-based protocols serialise through leader — bad for geo-distributed (cross-region latency). EPaxos: command coordinated by nearest replica. Used in some research + niche production.

sub_mechanisms.name: flexible_paxos
sub_mechanisms.definition: Heidi Howard 2016: quorums for phase 1 + phase 2 can differ. Only requirement: any phase-1 quorum intersects any phase-2 quorum.
sub_mechanisms.why: Asymmetric quorums: e.g., phase 2 (writes) needs 2 of 5; phase 1 (leader election) needs 4 of 5. Reduces write latency at cost of slower election. Used in some modern systems.

sub_mechanisms.name: CRDT
sub_mechanisms.definition: Conflict-free Replicated Data Types. Mathematical structures that converge regardless of update order.
sub_mechanisms.why: Eventual consistency without conflict resolution. Counter, set, map variants. Used in Redis CRDTs, Yjs (collaborative editing), Riak. Trade strong consistency for partition tolerance.

derivation_rules.name: majority_quorum_intersection_guarantees_safety
if: any two quorums of ⌈N/2⌉+1 must intersect
derivation_rules.why: New leader's election quorum overlaps with prior commit quorum → sees committed entries. Without intersection, two disjoint quorums could commit conflicting entries. The mathematical foundation of Raft + Paxos safety.

derivation_rules.name: FLP_requires_partial_synchrony_for_progress
then: no deterministic consensus tolerates one crash
derivation_rules.why: Fischer-Lynch-Paterson. Practical consensus uses timeouts (partial synchrony assumption) to make progress. Safety preserved without sync; liveness requires it. The fundamental compromise of practical consensus.

derivation_rules.name: Raft_easier_than_Paxos_at_same_safety
derivation_rules.why: Ongaro's design goal: easier-to-understand consensus. Strong leader + log structure + state-machine simulation. Same safety as Multi-Paxos but cleaner spec. Production systems (etcd, Consul, CockroachDB) adopt Raft for this.

derivation_rules.name: CRDTs_trade_consistency_for_availability
if: data type has commutative + associative + idempotent updates
derivation_rules.why: Counter: add operations commute. G-Set: union commutes. Updates apply locally + propagate; merges automatically resolve. No consensus needed; trade-off: eventual consistency instead of strong.

derivation_rules.name: Byzantine_needs_3f_plus_1_nodes
then: ≥3f+1 total nodes are required for safe consensus
derivation_rules.why: Quorum must exclude f Byzantine + tolerate f more crashed. Intersection argument with 2f+1 quorums on 3f+1 nodes. Bitcoin's proof-of-work, PBFT, HotStuff all respect this bound.
